references.text: Jacob also arranged his family with the weakest at the rear for protection, similar to how the tribe of Dan placed their children, livestock, and valuables in front of them.
Pharaoh discusses letting the Israelites go with their children and livestock, highlighting the importance of protecting families and property during movement.
The Gadites and Reubenites mention their children and livestock left behind in the cities of Gilead, showing a similar prioritization of family safety.
At the conquest of Jericho, everything in the city, including livestock, was devoted to destruction, contrasting with the Danites' desire to protect their livestock.
The continuation of this account where the Danites attack Laish shows the result of their strategic movement with families protected.
